Call GetRememberedPosition() after one or more calls to this method to retrieve the tracked position; calling it without a prior remembered position yields an implementation-defined/unknown value.
next_char may be a digit (ASCII or supported non-ASCII numeric forms) or a formatting character as allowed by the implementation.
The instance must have been obtained from PhoneNumberUtil::GetAsYouTypeFormatter() and be in a valid, non-destroyed state.
The class is not thread-safe; do not call concurrently from multiple threads.

The class is not thread-safe; do not call concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::GetSupportedRegions
functions.description: Populates the provided set with all CLDR two-letter region codes for which the library has metadata (geographical regions only).
requirements: regions must be a non-null pointer to a valid std::set<std::string> to receive results.
Region codes are returned in upper-case CLDR format.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::GetSupportedGlobalNetworkCallingCodes
functions.description: Populates the provided set with global network (non-geographical) country calling codes for which the library has metadata.
requirements: calling_codes must be non-null and point to a valid std::set<int> to receive results.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::GetSupportedCallingCodes
functions.description: Populates the provided set with all country calling codes supported by the library, including both geographical and non-geographical entities.
requirements: calling_codes must be non-null and point to a valid std::set<int> to receive results.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::GetSupportedTypesForRegion
functions.description: Returns, via the output set, the phone number types for which metadata exists for the specified region. Excludes FIXED_LINE_OR_MOBILE and UNKNOWN. Returns no types for invalid/unknown regions.
requirements: types must be non-null and point to a valid std::set<PhoneNumberType>.
region_code should be a valid upper-case CLDR two-letter region code; otherwise the output set will remain empty.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::GetSupportedTypesForNonGeoEntity
functions.description: Returns, via the output set, the number types supported for the given non‑geographical country calling code. Excludes FIXED_LINE_OR_MOBILE and UNKNOWN.
requirements: types must be non-null and point to a valid std::set<PhoneNumberType>.
country_calling_code must correspond to a known non‑geographical entity; otherwise no types are returned.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::GetInstance
functions.description: Returns the singleton PhoneNumberUtil instance, preloaded with commonly used regions' metadata. Multiple calls return the same instance.
requirements: None beyond standard singleton usage; caller must not delete the returned pointer.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::IsAlphaNumber
functions.description: Determines if the input represents a valid vanity (alpha) number (e.g., 800 MICROSOFT). Checks for at least 3 starting digits and three or more alphabetic characters; no region-specific validation.
requirements: number should be a phone-number-like string; formatting is allowed.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::ConvertAlphaCharactersInNumber
functions.description: Converts alphabetic characters in a phone number string to their corresponding keypad digits, preserving existing formatting.
requirements: number must be non-null and point to a mutable std::string to be modified in place.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::NormalizeDigitsOnly
functions.description: Normalizes a phone number string to digits by converting wide-ASCII and Arabic-Indic numerals to European digits and stripping punctuation and letters.
requirements: number must be non-null and point to a mutable std::string to be modified in place.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::NormalizeDiallableCharsOnly
functions.description: Strips all characters that are not diallable on a mobile keypad (including non-ASCII digits), leaving only characters that can be dialed.
requirements: number must be non-null and point to a mutable std::string to be modified in place.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::GetNationalSignificantNumber
functions.signature: void i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::GetNationalSignificantNumber(const i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumber& number, std::string* national_number) const
functions.description: Extracts the national significant number (NSN) from the given PhoneNumber (no national prefix or formatting) and writes it to the output string.
requirements: national_number must be non-null and point to a valid std::string to receive the result.
number should be a parsed PhoneNumber; behavior with incomplete/invalid numbers follows library semantics.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::GetLengthOfGeographicalAreaCode
functions.description: Returns the length of the geographical area code for the provided number to help split an NSN into area code and subscriber number. Not all numbers have area codes; returns 0 in such cases. Area-code definitions may change over time.
requirements: number should be a valid, parsed PhoneNumber for best results.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::GetLengthOfNationalDestinationCode
functions.description: Returns the length of the National Destination Code (NDC) for the provided number to split the NSN into NDC and subscriber number. Not all numbers have an NDC; returns 0 in such cases.
requirements: number should be a valid, parsed PhoneNumber for best results.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::GetCountryMobileToken
functions.description: Retrieves the mobile token for the given country calling code (if any). A mobile token is inserted before the area code when dialing a mobile number from abroad. Writes an empty string if none.
requirements: mobile_token must be non-null and point to a std::string to receive the result.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::Format
functions.signature: void i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::Format(const i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumber& number, i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::PhoneNumberFormat number_format, std::string* formatted_number) const
functions.description: Formats the given number using default rules into the specified format (E164, INTERNATIONAL, NATIONAL, or RFC3966). Not guaranteed to be directly diallable in all contexts.
requirements: formatted_number must be non-null and point to a std::string to receive the output.
number should be a parsed PhoneNumber; invalid numbers may yield best-effort formatting.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::FormatByPattern
functions.signature: void i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::FormatByPattern(const i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumber& number, i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::PhoneNumberFormat number_format, const ::google::protobuf::RepeatedPtrField<i18n::phonenumbers::NumberFormat>& user_defined_formats, std::string* formatted_number) const
functions.description: Formats the number in the specified format using client-supplied formatting patterns (NumberFormat).
requirements: formatted_number must be non-null and point to a std::string.
user_defined_formats should contain valid NumberFormat entries applicable to the number's region/type.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::FormatNationalNumberWithCarrierCode
functions.signature: void i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::FormatNationalNumberWithCarrierCode(const i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumber& number, const std::string& carrier_code, std::string* formatted_number) const
functions.description: Formats the number in national format inserting the specified carrier code for dialing. If carrier_code is empty, formats without a carrier code. Overrides any preferred domestic carrier code on the number.
requirements: formatted_number must be non-null and point to a std::string.
carrier_code may be empty to omit carrier code; otherwise should be a valid carrier selection string for the region.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::FormatNationalNumberWithPreferredCarrierCode
functions.signature: void i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::FormatNationalNumberWithPreferredCarrierCode(const i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumber& number, const std::string& fallback_carrier_code, std::string* formatted_number) const
functions.description: Formats the number in national format using the number's preferred_domestic_carrier_code if present; otherwise uses fallback_carrier_code. If both are absent/empty, formats without a carrier code.
requirements: formatted_number must be non-null.
fallback_carrier_code may be empty; otherwise should be valid for the region.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::FormatNumberForMobileDialing
functions.signature: void i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::FormatNumberForMobileDialing(const i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumber& number, const std::string& region_calling_from, bool with_formatting, std::string* formatted_number) const
functions.description: Produces a representation of the number that can be dialed from a mobile phone in a specific region. Returns empty string if unreachable from that region. Can optionally include formatting.
requirements: formatted_number must be non-null.
region_calling_from should be a valid CLDR region code.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::FormatOutOfCountryCallingNumber
functions.signature: void i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::FormatOutOfCountryCallingNumber(const i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumber& number, const std::string& calling_from, std::string* formatted_number) const

requirements: formatted_number must be non-null.
calling_from should be a valid CLDR region code.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::FormatInOriginalFormat
functions.signature: void i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::FormatInOriginalFormat(const i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumber& number, const std::string& region_calling_from, std::string* formatted_number) const
functions.description: Formats a number using the same style it was parsed with (if parsed via ParseAndKeepRawInput); otherwise uses NATIONAL format. Falls back to raw input for unknown/invalid cases.
requirements: formatted_number must be non-null.
For original-format behavior, the PhoneNumber must have been populated via ParseAndKeepRawInput.
region_calling_from may influence formatting; should be a valid CLDR code.

functions.name: i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::FormatOutOfCountryKeepingAlphaChars
functions.signature: void i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumberUtil::FormatOutOfCountryKeepingAlphaChars(const i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumber& number, const std::string& calling_from, std::string* formatted_number) const

proto_to_convert must be a valid, initialized i18n::phonenumbers::PhoneNumber; ideally a parsed or otherwise populated instance.
The function does not take ownership of either argument; caller retains ownership.

requirements: matched_string may be NULL; if non-null it must point to a valid std::string.
Check the boolean return value before using outputs.

functions.signature: virtual bool Replace(std::string* string_to_process, bool global, const std::string& replacement_string) const

functions.description: Constructs a RegExpCache that creates and caches RegExp objects using the provided AbstractRegExpFactory. The cache may pre-allocate or size itself based on min_items. Typical usage: create one cache per factory and reuse it to retrieve compiled regex objects by pattern.

functions.description: Destroys the RegExpCache and any cached RegExp objects it owns. After destruction, previously obtained references to RegExp from this cache become invalid.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for regular expression pattern strings tailored to libphonenumber usage.
# Goals:
# - Produce syntactically valid regexes across common engines (ICU/RE2-like subset).
# - Cover a breadth of constructs used by libphonenumber metadata and tests:
#   - digit classes, quantifiers, groups, alternations, anchors
#   - simple capture groups for formatting patterns (e.g., (\d{2,4})(\d+))
#   - leading digits patterns (e.g., ^(?:1|2|[3-5])
#   - national number patterns like ^[0-9]{min,max}$
#   - optional separators and literal escapes
# - Keep length reasonable (< 4096 bytes; typically much smaller).

DIGIT_CLASSES = [r"\d", r"[0-9]", r"[1-9]", r"[2-9]", r"[0-8]"]
SEP_CLASSES = [r"[ .-]", r"[\s-]", r"[\s]", r"[- ]", r"[\u00A0 ]"]
LITERAL_SEPS = [" ", "-", "."]
ANCHORS = ["^", ""]
END_ANCHORS = ["$", ""]

# Safe, commonly-supported quantifiers (avoid pathological/backtracking-heavy forms)
QUANTS_SIMPLE = ["", "?", "+", "*"]


def _q_range(min_n: int, max_n: int) -> str:
    if min_n == max_n:
        return f"{{{min_n}}}"
    return f"{{{min_n},{max_n}}}"


def _rand_digit_atom(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Randomly choose between a class or explicit class range
    choice = rng.randrange(5)
    if choice <= 3:
        return rng.choice(DIGIT_CLASSES)
    # Explicit custom class like [2-9] or [0-3]
    a = rng.randint(0, 9)
    b = rng.randint(0, 9)
    if a > b:
        a, b = b, a
    if a == b:
        return f"[{a}]"
    return f"[{a}-{b}]"


def _rand_sep(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(SEP_CLASSES + LITERAL_SEPS + [""])


def _group(seq: str, non_capturing: bool) -> str:
    if non_capturing:
        return f"(?:{seq})"
    else:
        return f"({seq})"


def _build_national_number_pattern(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Typical pattern: ^[0-9]{n}$ or a small range allowing prefixes
    n = rng.randint(2, 12)
    span = rng.randint(0, min(4, n - 1)) if n > 1 else 0
    min_len = max(1, n - span)
    max_len = n
    cls = rng.choice([r"[0-9]", r"\d"])
    return f"^{cls}{_q_range(min_len, max_len)}$"


def _build_leading_digits_pattern(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Patterns used for leading digits: anchored prefix with alternatives
    # Example: ^(?:1|2|[3-5]) or ^(?:2|23|234)
    alts: List[str] = []
    count = rng.randint(2, 5)
    for _ in range(count):
        form = rng.randrange(3)
        if form == 0:
            # single digit
            alts.append(str(rng.randint(0, 9)))
        elif form == 1:
            # short literal prefix like 23 or 234
            length = rng.randint(1, 3)
            alts.append("".join(str(rng.randint(0, 9)) for _ in range(length)))
        else:
            # class range
            a = rng.randint(0, 9)
            b = rng.randint(0, 9)
            if a > b:
                a, b = b, a
            if a == b:
                alts.append(f"[{a}]")
            else:
                alts.append(f"[{a}-{b}]")
    body = "|".join(alts)
    return f"^(?:{body})"


def _build_format_capture_pattern(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Patterns intended for formatting with backrefs, e.g.: (\d{2,4})(\d+)
    # We build 2-4 capture groups separated by optional separators.
    groups = rng.randint(2, 4)
    parts: List[str] = []
    for i in range(groups):
        atom = _rand_digit_atom(rng)
        if atom in (r"\d", r"[0-9]"):
            # Prefer bounded ranges to avoid catastrophic growth
            if i == 0:
                q = _q_range(rng.randint(1, 3), rng.randint(3, 6))
            else:
                # Allow unbounded tail sometimes
                if rng.random() < 0.3:
                    q = "+"
                else:
                    q = _q_range(rng.randint(1, 2), rng.randint(3, 8))
        else:
            # For narrow classes, use + or {m}
            q = rng.choice(["+", _q_range(rng.randint(1, 3), rng.randint(3, 6))])
        parts.append(_group(f"{atom}{q}", non_capturing=False))
        if i != groups - 1:
            sep = _rand_sep(rng)
            if sep:
                parts.append(sep)
    # Optional anchors
    pre = rng.choice(ANCHORS)
    post = rng.choice(END_ANCHORS)
    return f"{pre}{''.join(parts)}{post}"


def _build_alt_blocks_pattern(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Alternation of different block lengths with optional separators
    # Example: ^(?:\d{3}|\d{2})[- ]?\d{4}$
    a1 = _group(rf"\d{rng.randint(2,4)}", non_capturing=True)
    a2 = _group(rf"\d{{{rng.randint(2,3)},{rng.randint(4,6)}}}", non_capturing=True)
    alt = f"(?:{a1}|{a2})"
    tail = rf"{_rand_sep(rng)}\d{{{rng.randint(2,4)},{rng.randint(4,8)}}}"
    return f"^{alt}{tail}$"


def _build_misc_safe_pattern(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # A generic safe pattern combining atoms and quantifiers
    length = rng.randint(2, 5)
    seq: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(length):
        atom = _rand_digit_atom(rng)
        q = rng.choice(QUANTS_SIMPLE + [ _q_range(rng.randint(1,3), rng.randint(3,6)) ])
        seq.append(f"{atom}{q}")
        # Occasionally insert a non-capturing group or alternation of small atoms
        if rng.random() < 0.25:
            x = _rand_digit_atom(rng)
            y = _rand_digit_atom(rng)
            seq.append(f"(?:{x}|{y})")
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            seq.append(_rand_sep(rng))
    pre = rng.choice(ANCHORS)
    post = rng.choice(END_ANCHORS)
    return f"{pre}{''.join(seq)}{post}"


def _choose_pattern(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    builders = [
        _build_national_number_pattern,
        _build_leading_digits_pattern,
        _build_format_capture_pattern,
        _build_alt_blocks_pattern,
        _build_misc_safe_pattern,
    ]
    # Weighted selection to favor commonly used shapes
    weights = [3, 2, 3, 2, 2]
    total = sum(weights)
    pick = rng.randint(1, total)
    acc = 0
    for b, w in zip(builders, weights):
        acc += w
        if pick <= acc:
            return b(rng)
    return builders[0](rng)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Compose possibly multiple lines/patterns to seed different fuzz sites; however, engines
    # typically compile a single pattern string. We'll occasionally emit a single robust pattern,
    # or a concise one. Ensure size under 4096 bytes.
    patterns: List[str] = []
    count = 1 if rng.random() < 0.8 else rng.randint(2, 3)
    for _ in range(count):
        p = _choose_pattern(rng)
        patterns.append(p)
    # Join multiple patterns with a newline so each consumer that expects a single pattern
    # still gets one line (first line), while others that accept more arbitrary text can use more.
    out = "\n".join(patterns)
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]
    return out.encode("utf-8")

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: alphabetic string (A-Z letters only)
# The stubs extract only alphabetic characters and build 2-letter uppercase
# region codes. They also use FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for phone number raw inputs,
# but our guidance focuses on providing interesting alphabetic strings that
# result in meaningful region codes across many paths.
#
# Strategy:
# - Emit sequences of plausible 2-letter region codes (US, GB, CA, AU, DE, FR, JP, CN, IN, BR, RU, ZA, NZ, KR, MX, IT, ES, SE, NO, DK, NL, BE, CH, AT, IE).
# - Mix in longer alphabetic strings containing multiple potential region codes
#   so that different calls to FUZZ_PARAM_STR() can extract different pairs.
# - Include lowercase variants since the stubs uppercase them.
# - Interleave separators and non-letters sparingly? The data type definition
#   says alphabetic only, so we will stick to letters to maximize extraction.
# - Keep output <= 4096 bytes.
# - Randomize order and casing deterministically by seed.
#
# Although many FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls consume general strings (e.g., phone
# numbers), providing region-like alphabetic strings ensures sanitizers pick
# valid 2-letter codes and exercise more code paths (example-number retrieval,
# NANPA checks, etc.).

_COMMON_REGIONS = [
    "US","GB","CA","AU","DE","FR","JP","CN","IN","BR",
    "RU","ZA","NZ","KR","MX","IT","ES","SE","NO","DK",
    "NL","BE","CH","AT","IE","PT","GR","TR","PL","CZ",
    "SK","HU","RO","BG","UA","BY","FI","IS","EE","LV",
    "LT","SI","HR","BA","RS","ME","MK","AL","MD","GE",
    "AM","AZ","KZ","UZ","TM","KG","TJ","SG","MY","TH",
    "VN","PH","ID","HK","MO","TW","KR","KP","SA","AE",
    "IL","EG","KE","NG","GH","CM","ET","TZ","UG","AR",
    "CL","CO","PE","VE","UY","PY","BO","EC","PA","CR",
    "DO","GT","HN","NI","SV","JM","CU","PR","QA","KW",
]

def _rand_case(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Randomize casing per character (alphabetic only)
    out_chars = []
    for ch in s:
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            out_chars.append(ch.lower())
        else:
            out_chars.append(ch.upper())
    return ''.join(out_chars)

def _build_alphabetic_stream(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> str:
    # Build a stream of alphabetic tokens, emphasizing valid region pairs first
    regions = _COMMON_REGIONS.copy()
    rng.shuffle(regions)
    parts: List[str] = []

    # Start with several valid 2-letter region codes to seed early consumers
    for rc in regions[:max(10, min(len(regions), count//4))]:
        parts.append(_rand_case(rng, rc))

    # Add mixed runs containing multiple region-like pairs concatenated
    for _ in range(max(5, count//6)):
        run_len = rng.randint(2, 8)  # number of pairs to join
        run = ''.join(_rand_case(rng, rng.choice(regions)) for _ in range(run_len))
        parts.append(run)

    # Add some random alphabetic noise blocks to vary extraction
    for _ in range(max(3, count//10)):
        n = rng.randint(3, 20)
        noise = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(n))
        parts.append(noise)

    # Finish with a few specific interesting pairs
    tail = ["US","ZZ","CA","GB","JP","CN","IN"]
    # Note: "ZZ" isn't a real region in CLDR list for most APIs, but the
    # sanitizers may fallback; still keep alphabetic-only per type.
    for rc in tail:
        parts.append(_rand_case(rng, rc))

    rng.shuffle(parts)
    s = ''.join(parts)
    # Ensure we have at least some immediate valid leading pairs
    prefix = ''.join(_rand_case(rng, rc) for rc in regions[:5])
    return prefix + s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose an approximate complexity level for how many segments to include
    count = rng.randint(30, 80)
    s = _build_alphabetic_stream(rng, count)
    # Clip to 4096 bytes max
    if len(s) > 4096:
        s = s[:4096]
    return s.encode('ascii')
